newsitem.title: USA: HOT STOCK HIGHLIGHTS - U.S. Corporate Earnings.
newsitem.headline: HOT STOCK HIGHLIGHTS - U.S. Corporate Earnings.

text.p: Shares slightly higher in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange with over two million shares changing hands after the maker of computer products said it is on its way toward delivering full-year profitability in 1997.
The company posted a better-than-expected Q1 loss per share of $0.06 compared with $0.25 last year. According to First Call, analysts expected the company to lose $0.14 a share.

Shares lower in afternoon trading after the telephone giant reported weak Q1 EPS of $0.69 a share compared with $0.85. Although the earnings matched analysts' expectations, the company said it expects slightly weaker second quarter results. Merrill Lynch cut 1997 and 1998 profit estimates and other analysts polled said they planned to do the same.
Shares slipped after the company posted Q1 EPS of $0.44 a share versus $0.35 last year after the market close on Friday.
Stock more than 17 percent after the company posted better than expected second quarter earnings but said it was behind in its plan to expend capacity to make TSA suspensions.
Company earned $0.91 a share, better than estimates of $0.88 a share, compared to $0.26 in the year-ago quarter. The second fiscal quarter ended March 30, 1997.

Shares rise more than 16 percent after the outdoor sporting goods wholesaler posted first quarter earnings rose to $0.08 compared to $0.07 last year. Sales eked higher to $36.8 million from $36.7 million.

Maker of business forms for auto dealers, office products dealer, slipped ten percent after the company said it earned $0.31 a share for the fiscal second quarter ended March 31, a penny shy of estimates. The company earned to $0.27 in the year-ago period. Sales higher, jumping to $354.2 million from $257.0 million last year.
